title: Macquarie Bank Faces $14m Fine over Promotion of Savings Account Rates to New Customers
body:
This ABC article discusses this current fine and also the previous fine.
"$8.8 million in remediation initiated by Macquarie which has already been paid to nearly 40,000 customers"
"Macquarie Bank said it would not contest the ASIC proceeding and is expected to pay a $14 million civil penalty"
"It said the ASIC announcement related to products offered on its website between December 2021 and September 2022"
Out of curiosity, did any Ozbargainers here take up this Macquarie deal between those dates and receive remediation payments?
I was initially confused about the allegations of misleading customers as I, and presumably the rest of Ozbargain, have never highlighted any issues with the marketing and communication of Macquarie's savings account and welcome rate for new customers. That was until I realised the issue was from about 5 years ago.
I discovered Macquarie through Ozbargain and they have been great. Macquarie has apologised for the confusion caused. All the banks should learn from this mistake and give us clear and precise communication, particularly in light of the number of hoops in their HISAs and the sometimes convoluted T&C.
